set.grade.domains.risk_of_bias.note: Downgraded one level under METHODS §6.3 (a claim seen only through reviews: the cohorts were not read, so their risk of bias is not appraisable, and the one review is rated critically low by AMSTAR 2). The per-cohort data the review prints, the same direction in all 16 methadone cohorts, and adjusted ratios unchanged or larger in six cohorts are why it is not downgraded further.
set.grade.reasoning: Cohort studies are observational and start low; downgraded one level for risk of bias because the claim is seen only through one review, rated critically low, and the cohorts themselves were not read (METHODS §6.3, claims seen only through reviews): very low. Not downgraded further: the review prints each cohort's data, the direction holds in all 16 methadone cohorts for all causes and all 11 for overdose, and adjustment in six cohorts left the ratios unchanged or larger. The start of methadone treatment (not statistically significant), the buprenorphine figures (three cohorts, mostly one Australian study) and the overdose figures by period (three cohorts) are worded as uncertain and not rated separately. Whether treatment prevents deaths, or stopping causes them, is not claimed. Status: replicated (16 methadone cohorts from different countries and teams, same direction); one review read.
